weeks.say: Counting note: these plates were counted as ranges, 100 to 140 and 70 to 100 colonies, and the plate counts shown are the midpoints. On the full ranges the value could be anywhere from about 1,020 to 1,440 CFU/100 mL, red either way. Method note: the plated volume was five pipette draws with water reaching the bulb. Calibrated afterwards against a test tube, three such draws consistently measure 5 mL, so each plate received about 8.3 mL and the value here uses the measured volume (multiplier 12, not the nominal 20). The red call is unchanged. Draws are stopped at the 1 mL stem mark from week 3 on. Incubation note: the plate spent about an hour at room temperature before the incubator, close to the usual gel-set wait, then 24 hours at 35 C as planned. The count is not expected to be affected.

Counting note: these plates were counted from backlit photographs, not directly off the plates. Photo counts proved unreliable in weeks 3 and 4, one too high and one too low, so this week's value, and its comparison with the laboratory split below, carry that extra uncertainty. First reading from the project’s own rain gauge at the boathouse: 0.00 in in the 48 hours before the sample, so this week’s number is no longer attributed to an airport three miles away. Plated volume was confirmed at a true 5 mL, so the standard multiplier of 20 applies with no correction needed. The plate counts shown are the sampler’s own direct count off the physical plates (16 and 11), which replaced an earlier photograph-based estimate (approximately 28 and 22) that ran high, likely from misjudging colony color under backlight rather than plain white light.

The rain landed inside this week’s 48 hour window for the first time this season: 1.20 in on the sample day itself, from the project’s own gauge, with the water level visibly raised by flooding on top of a low, ebbing tide. Turbidity dropped to 14.25 cm, the murkiest reading of the season by a wide margin. The plate counts (145 and 150) are the sampler’s own direct count off the physical plates.

Turbidity reached 82 cm, the clearest reading of the season to that point. Two gauge readings before the sample, 0.10 in and 0.18 in, add up to 0.28 in of antecedent rain, the second logged under the following calendar day but confirmed to have fallen before this sample. Plate counts (23 and 30) are the sampler’s own direct count off the physical plates.

Turbidity reached 92 cm, clearer than week 5’s 82 cm. The 48 hour antecedent rain is 0.00 in, which makes this a dry week by the site’s own rule, but the gauge logged 1.25 in on 27 September, 1.11 in on 28 September and 0.15 in on 29 September, 2.51 in in all, in the days before the window opened. A week like this is why the 48 hour figure needs the full rain log beside it. Plate counts (32 and 29) are the sampler’s own direct count off the physical plates. This was a laboratory split sample, taken on a Friday morning; the laboratory result is pending and will be added when it arrives.

Turbidity reached 96 cm, the clearest reading of the season to that point. The 48 hour antecedent rain figure is a minimum, not an exact number: 0.58 in was read at 9:00 on 11 October, before the sample, and 2.50 in was read at noon on 12 October, a reading that covers hours both before and after the 5:45 PM sample. The sampler confirmed that some of it fell before the sample and some after but did not record how much, so the true figure is above 0.58 in by an unknown amount. Either way this is a wet week. There is no sample for the week of 4 October; the previous one was the 2 October laboratory split. Plate counts (44 and 50) are the sampler’s own direct count off the physical plates.

Water temperature fell to 14.2 C (57.5 F), the coldest of the season, and turbidity read 95 cm, nearly matching last week’s season-clearest 96 cm. The 48 hour antecedent rain is 0.34 in, read on 17 October and confirmed by the sampler to have fallen after 5 PM on 16 October; the 0.05 in read at 7:40 on 16 October came before the window opened, and the gauge read 0.00 in on 18 October. Plate counts (45 and 40) are the sampler’s own direct count off the physical plates. Both plates also carried many brown or olive colonies, a color not seen on earlier plates; they are not counted as E. coli. No laboratory split was sent this week.

This sample was taken at 7:15 on a Monday morning, not the usual Sunday evening, so it is not a like-for-like comparison with earlier weeks on time of day. Water temperature fell to 12.2 C (54 F), the coldest of the season. Turbidity read 66 cm, down from 95 cm last week and the murkiest reading since week 4, even though the sampler reports no rain at all during the week; the 48 hour antecedent rain is recorded as 0.00 in on that report. Plate counts (30 and 25) are the sampler’s own direct count off the physical plates. No laboratory split was sent this week.
